html:
The Mongol invasions of Georgia began in 1220, when Mongol scouts under Jebe and Subutai crushed the Georgian army of King George IV, son of Tamar. In 1236 a full Mongol army conquered the country.

In between, the Khwarazmian ruler Jalal ad-Din sacked Tbilisi in 1226. Under Queen Rusudan Georgia became a vassal of the Mongols, paying tribute and sending troops to their wars. The kingdom split between rival kings in east and west. King George V the Brilliant reunited it and threw off the Mongol yoke in the 1330s, but the Black Death and the invasions of Timur in the late 1300s ruined it again. Georgia broke into several kingdoms and principalities by the 1490s.
